summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas transplant, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, chronic heart failure, and severe orthostatic hypotension was admitted for chills, low-grade fever, and hypotension. She was found to have stable vital signs without evidence of active infection, as blood, urine, and peritoneal fluid cultures were negative. Her hypotension was attributed to excessive fluid removal during peritoneal dialysis, and antibiotics were discontinued after no infectious source was identified. Imaging showed pleural effusions and pulmonary edema, with echocardiography revealing moderate to severe mitral regurgitation and reduced left ventricular function. Her CD4 count was low at 165, but she remained on appropriate prophylactic medications. Warfarin was adjusted to 1 mg daily due to prior supratherapeutic INR and ongoing clotting risk. She improved clinically, was weaned off vasopressors, and transitioned back to extended care with follow-up planned in cardiology for mitral valve evaluation.
